problem: Existing EQA agents use VLMs to explore and answer directly without explicit thinking or planning, so they answer before finding all relevant objects and take redundant, inefficient exploration routes.
motivation: EQA needs both accurate answers and short exploration. Explicit multi-step reasoning plus tools that supply fine-grained information (3D boxes, crops, localization) should guide better next-step exploration. Training such reasoning needs tool-usage trajectory data, which does not exist for EQA.
key_idea: Treat the physical environment (GoNextPoint) and perception tools as a unified tool set, so a planner-controller-executor agent reasons step by step and writes code to call tools, then fine-tune the controller on an automatically generated EQA reasoning-trajectory dataset (EQA-RT).
insight: Fine-tuning on the synthetic trajectories lifts Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 45.1 to 56.1 success on EQA-RT-Unseen open-vocabulary, above GPT-4o (49.3). Fine-tuning also raises thought length (90.26 to 116.15) and correct tool-call rate (58 to 69), which suggests the gain comes from better reasoning and tool use. Tool-based reasoning mainly shortens exploration: on HM-EQA path length is 18.26 m against 30-39 m for baselines, at comparable accuracy.
method: Planner: an LLM reads the question once and decomposes it into structured sub-goals, to prevent blind exploration.

Controller: a VLM takes the question, history (thought, code, observation) and plan, and outputs a thought plus Python code each step. It handles three cases: missing objects (pick a direction via GoNextPoint), object visible but info insufficient (call tools), and info sufficient (compute and call FinalAnswer).
Executor: runs the code with real tools: GoNextPoint, ObjectLocation2D, ObjectLocation3D, ObjectCrop, VisualQA, SegmentInstance and FinalAnswer, to obtain new observations.

EQA task generation: a 3D detector gives object boxes, positions and categories in 713 HM3D scenes. GPT-4o generates Q&A over six types (relationship, status, distance, location, counting, attribute), in open-ended or multiple-choice form.
Trajectory generation: shortest path over the question's objects with A*, then GPT-4o adds thoughts and tool code per step. Key steps (target found) and non-key steps use type-specific prompts.

Verification: a task verifier (Grounded-SAM confidence plus GPT-4o similarity score) and a trajectory verifier (rule checks on tools and parameters plus GPT-4o checks for consistency and hallucination) filter the data.

Training: SFT with cross-entropy on thought and code only (final answer not fitted), LoRA on the language model with the vision encoder frozen. Trajectory sampling keeps all key steps plus an equal number of random non-key steps.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B controller (LoRA fine-tuned); zero-shot variants use GPT-4o or Qwen2.5-VL-7B; LLM planner
setting.training_data: EQA-RT-Train, part of the ~18K auto-generated EQA tasks with GPT-4o reasoning trajectories over HM3D scenes; SFT with LoRA, 4 H100 for 2 days
setting.observation: egocentric RGB images (plus tool outputs such as 2D/3D boxes, depth-based object 3D locations)
setting.action_space: tool calls via generated code; GoNextPoint with a direction such as 'turn left' selecting the next exploration point
setting.privileged: 3D object localization tool (ObjectLocation3D) returns 3D boxes and centers; no GT map stated

results: On EQA-RT-Unseen, fine-tuned ToolEQA (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) reaches 59.5 (multi-choice) and 56.1 (open vocabulary) success against Memory-EQA at 48.9 and 35.9, and beats zero-shot GPT-4o ToolEQA. On HM-EQA it gets 62.3 success at 18.26 m, versus Graph-EQA at 63.5 and Memory-EQA at 63.4 with 33.54 m. On EXPRESS-Bench it beats Fine-EQA (42.21 vs 40.55 Succ, 25.82 vs 16.22 E_path).
limitations: Heavy inference cost: controller uses about 9.5K tokens, 25.4 s and 40.5 GB per step, and the average trajectory has about 12 steps.
Training data and verifiers rely on GPT-4o and 3D detection outputs, so label quality is bounded by them. Tools such as ObjectLocation3D depend on 3D perception.
Accuracy on HM-EQA is only comparable to prior methods (62.3 vs 63.5); the gain there is mainly path length. Simulation only.
